players.product: bring-your-own-power combined-cycle gas generation for hyperscale data centers (1.2 GW Texas project; 5.4 GW of GE Vernova turbine / Kiewit EPC slots)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (CFO): adjusted EBITDA $1.08 billion, adjusted net income $308 million and adjusted EPS $1.49; adjusted EBITDA was lower by $46 million year over year on mild Texas weather and Winter Storm Fern supply costs in the East, partly offset by the LS Power portfolio (closed January 30th, approximately 2 months of contribution). Management reaffirmed 2026 guidance ranges and said the business remains on track for at least 14% adjusted EPS and free cash flow per share growth over the next five years before any contribution from large load or incremental development.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA $1.08 billion; adjusted net income $308 million; adjusted EPS $1.49; lower by $46 million YoY; at least 14% EPS/FCF per share growth

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on AI-driven power demand in ERCOT: 'This quarter's earnings season reinforced the scale of investment being directed toward AI infrastructure, and the implications for power demand are significant.' ERCOT's all-time peak demand is more than 85 gigawatts while the preliminary long-term load forecast shows large load requests reaching over 367 gigawatts by 2033; Senate Bill 6 and the large load batch process include bring-your-own-generation support, which management said aligns new demand with new supply.
quarterly_data.figure: ERCOT peak more than 85 gigawatts; large load requests over 367 gigawatts by 2033

quarterly_data.signal: Data center deal status: management's primary focus is front-of-the-meter generation for data centers ('The conversations that we have today, are front-of-the-meter conversations'), with behind-the-meter also considered; the previously discussed 90 to 95 was described as the top end for a normal data center deal, with prices that 'could go up depending on the environment' (an analyst cited behind-the-meter deals 'in the $150 range'; management did not adopt that number). CEO: 'We're getting to a place now, where we're going to get something done quickly.'
quarterly_data.figure: 90 to 95 was the top end for a normal data center deal

quarterly_data.signal: Timing and gating items for the data center deal: 'To hit 29, we've got to get something done in 2026.' Economics are 'pretty straightforward'; the remaining work is 'around infrastructure. Think interconnections for gen and load' plus gas infrastructure depending on site, involving regulated entities. In ERCOT the SB 6 rules are 'pretty well developed' and not 'the long pole in the tent'. NRG said its partnership with GEV and Kiewit gives it construction capability, equipment access and execution readiness, that it can take the GE turbines to PJM or anywhere 'for the right economics with the right counterparty', and that it can procure long-term gas through its midstream/upstream relationships if the customer wants it.

PJM expansion options: within the existing fleet NRG sees up to 2 gigawatts of upgrade and conversion opportunities, an incremental 1 gigawatt above the previously disclosed CT to CCGT conversion opportunity, mostly from the acquired LS Power assets. These can go through PJM's reliability backstop / long-term procurement or bilaterally; CEO: the auction 'priced right with the right rules, that's a great way to put 2 gigawatts of uprates into our fleet' or 'I can also have a conversation with a hyperscaler and put 1 gigawatt of that in at the same time'. NRG will not put capital to work in PJM on a merchant basis without contracts or long-term revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 2 gigawatts of upgrade and conversion opportunities; incremental 1 gigawatt; 1 gigawatt of that to a hyperscaler bilateral

quarterly_data.signal: New-build execution: the first Texas Energy Fund project, T.H. Wharton, was expected to come online in May, on time, on cost, and on spec (remaining step: syncing units to the grid and ERCOT confirmation); the three TEF projects total 1.5 GW, with Cedar Bayou and Greens Bayou at various stages of construction and on track for a 2028 COD.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.5 GW (three TEF projects); Cedar Bayou and Greens Bayou 2028 COD

quarterly_data.signal: Flexible load platform: NRG's Texas residential Virtual Power Plant is targeting 1 gigawatt of capacity (built on its retail and Smart Home businesses), and the CPower demand-response business adds C&I load management that management said could also be offered in PJM. Smart Home ended the quarter with approximately 2.37 million customers, up 9% year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: VPP targeting 1 gigawatt; approximately 2.37 million Smart Home customers (year-over-year increase of 9%)

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and capital allocation (CFO): on April 28 NRG closed $3.5 billion of new financing, retiring the $1.5 billion Lightning Power, LLC senior secured notes and reducing revolver borrowings (post-acquisition deleveraging toward a 3 times net leverage target); through April 30th, 2026 it completed $817 million in share repurchases, remains on track to return at least $1.4 billion to shareholders, and directs $310 million toward growth investments.
quarterly_data.figure: $3.5 billion new financing; $1.5 billion Lightning Power notes retired; $817 million repurchases; at least $1.4 billion capital return; $310 million growth investments
